newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., tightens seaport controls.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., tightens seaport controls.

text.p: Florida's Dade County Commission has tightened its oversight of promotinal spending at the fiscally ailing Port of Miami.

In a unanimous vote on Tuesday, the commission approved an ordinance requiring a written recommendation from the county manager and a two-thirds vote by the commission for all expenditures from the port's promotional fund.
No money could be spent from the fund without evidence showing how the promotional event would publicize the seaport.

Previously, only expenditures over $5,000 required commission scrutiny. The change follows disclosures that port revenues were frequently used for promotional events such as golf tournaments and neighborhood festivals unrelated to the port.

The expenditures were often made by commissioners, in the belief that the seaport was flush with money. The commission discovered last week that the facility had a $22 million cash flow deficit and had borrowed money from the county's general fund budget to keep operating.
The commission also rejected a proposal by County Manager Armando Vidal to raise the local gasoline tax by one cent per gallon.

Without the new revenue, Vidal said the county would have to raise transit fees, cut transit services or dip into its newly created contingency reserve fund for the criminal justice system. Doing so would reduce the fund's proposed $5 million allocation for fiscal 1998 to $1.1 million.
